chunk-001:c001.proposition: Every human action results from an unbroken chain of prior causes, leaving no genuinely available alternative selected through free will.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Choices reflect interacting causes extending from immediate neural and hormonal conditions through development, environment, culture, ancestry, and evolution.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Biological and environmental influences form a seamless interacting causal arc that leaves no behaviorally effective space for independent free will.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Felt choice cannot establish free will because historical errors, unconscious influences, and experimental findings show that intuitive explanations of behavior are unreliable.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Determinism permits learning, deliberation, and behavioral change because people are altered by mechanistic processes without freely choosing the process of change.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: Long-run consequential analysis condemns framing innocent people because permitting that practice causes wider institutional harm, without requiring retributive desert.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Scientific explanation has repeatedly displaced blame and punitive retribution for misunderstood behavior while producing more humane treatment rather than social collapse.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: Mechanistic testing exposes false intuitions, and existing evidence of reduced freedom in morally important domains warrants revising responsibility judgments.

chunk-003:c003-02.proposition: Behavior continues to have prior causes, while microscopic quantum indeterminacy cannot scale into person-level control over which action occurs.
